full_judgment:
2. Facts necessary for disposal of these petitions are that the petitioner filed an application before the Administrative Tribunal under section 4 of the Administrative Tribunal Act, 1980) (at the relevant time, there was only one Tribunal) impleading the respondents herein as opposite parties for declaration that the order as contained in Memo No.Sec-2/ Misc-19/2000/4931Edu dated 18-7-2001 passed by opposite party No. 1, respondent No. I herein (hereinafter referred to as opposite party No. 1), rejecting the appeal and the order contained in Memo No. DIA/99/1-C- 18/Admn-Part 11/417/6 dated 30-3-2000 passed by opposite party No.2, respondent No.2 herein (hereinafter referred to as opposite party No.2), dismissing the petitioner from service as illegal, void, not binding upon him, and he is still in service and also for a direction upon the opposite parties to reinstate him in service and give him all attending benefits admissible under the Rules. The application was registered as Administrative Tribunal Case No.2002 of 2001. Eventually the case was transferred to Administrative Tribunal No.2, Dhaka and was renumbered as Administrative Tribunal Case No. 192 of 2003. 

 3. The case of the petitioner was that he joined the service on 1-9-1971 as Lower Division Assistant under the Education Directorate, erstwhile East Pakistan. The petitioner since then had been serving honestly and diligently to the satisfaction of the higher authority, and due to his good performance in the service, he was promoted to the post of Upper Division Assistant on 4-5-1987 and to the post of Auditor on 18-2-1985. The petitioner while serving as Auditor in the Directorate of Inspection and Audit, there was serious dissatisfaction amongst the officers and the employees against Mr Atahar Ali Dewan, Director of Inspection and Audit, and subsequently, the petitioner along with other five employees was placed under suspension by the said Director of Inspector and Audit. While the petitioner was serving in the Directorate of Inspector and Audit, he received a charge sheet containing 19 charges on the allegations of misconduct, negligence of duty, inefficiency, unruliness etc. The petitioner was asked to show cause as to why he shall-not be dismissed from service. The petitioner filed an application on 1-9-1999 requesting the authority to supply him certain papers for taking proper defence, but copies of the papers sought were not supplied to him. Thereafter, the petitioner submitted his written defence denying the allegations made in the charge sheet, but the authority without considering the written defence of the petitioner constituted a Board of Inquiry on 1-9-1999 consisting of 3(three) members headed by Dr Md Abdul Motaleb; Deputy Director (Dhaka Division) as its Chairman. The petitioner and others filed an application to the Chairman of the Board of Inquiry with specific allegation of no confidence against the Chairman and one of the members of that Board, but no action was taken in that regard. However, the petitioner being directed by the Board of Inquiry, appeared before the Inquiry Officer along with defence witnesses. The Board of Inquiry recorded the statements of the petitioner and his witnesses in between 7-11-1999 to 18-11-1999 in the absence of the complainant, or any conducting officer on behalf of the prosecution. The petitioner was not also given any opportunity by the Inquiry Officer to consult the relevant papers. The Board of Inquiry also recorded the statements of the prosecution witnesses behind the back of the petitioner and he was not allowed to cross examine the witnesses adduced against him. The Board of Inquiry most illegally took statements beyond the knowledge of the petitioner, and accordingly, they submitted a perverse and frivolous report finding him guilty of the charge brought against him. Opposite party No.2 on the basis, of the illegal inquiry report issued the 2nd show cause notice upon the petitioner proposing major penalty of dismissal from service under rule 4(2)(d) of the Government Servants (Discipline and Appeal) Rules, 1985 and accordingly, on receipt of the 2nd show cause notice, the petitioner submitted his written reply to the authority on 16-2-2000 pleading his innocence, but opposite party No.2 most illegally and without lawful authority passed the impugned order on 30-3-2000 dismissing the petitioner from service. 

 5. Opposite party No.1 (before the Administrative Tribunal) contested the case by filing a written statement denying the material allegations made in the application and contending, inter alia, that the case was not maintainable in its present form, there was no cause of action to file the case, the case was bad for defect of party and it was also barred by limitation. A serious dissatisfaction arose amongst the employees, and the then Director Atahar Ali Dewan on different matters and the employees informed the matter to the Ministry of Education, but at one stage five employees including the petitioner were placed under suspension by the said Director on the allegation of misconduct. Charge was framed against the petitioner asking him to show cause is as to why he would not be dismissed from service. Accordingly, the petitioner showed his-cause in writing, but was not being satisfactory, the concerned-authority constituted a Board of Inquiry consisting there-members headed by Dr. Md Abdul Motaleb Deputy Director as Chairman of that committee. The Board of inquiry held inquiry from 8-9-1999 to 30-1-2000 giving opportunity to the petitioner of self-defence and submitted its report finding him guilty of the charges brought against him. Thereafter, the authority issued the 2nd show cause notice upon the petitioner proposing major penalty. The petitioner submitted his written reply to the show cause notice. The authority passed the impugned order dismissing the petitioner from service by observing all requirements of law. Against the order of dismissal, the petitioner filed departmental appeal to the Secretary, Ministry of Education and it was rejected after due consideration. There was no irregularity and illegality in the departmental proceeding and, as such, the impugned order passed by the authority was quite legal which did not call for any interference by the tribunal. The case of the petitioner was totally misconceived and thus it was liable to be dismissed. 

 9. Mr Sirajul Hoque relying on the 3rd proviso to sub-section (2) of section 4 of the Act, 1980 has submitted that since in the instant case, the appeal filed by the petitioner was formally rejected on 18-7-2001 that should be date of the cause of action to file the application before the Administrative Tribunal, but the Appellate Tribunal wrongly counted the date of limitation from the date of expiry of two months from the date of filing the departmental appeal before the appellate authority as provided in the 2nd proviso to sub-section (2) and thus acted illegally in dismissing the appeal on the ground of limitation and, as such, the impugned decision is not sustainable in law. 

 10. This Court in a number of cases earlier decided that it is the 2nd proviso to sub-section (2) of section 4 of the Act, 1980 read with the period of limitation as mentioned in the 3rd proviso, i.e. two months plus six months which shall govern the period of limitation in filing an application before the Administrative Tribunal and a case filed before the Administrative Tribunal after the expiry of the said period (two months + six months) shall be barred by limitation. 

 11. We do not see any reason to review the said decision of this Court. Therefore, we find nothing wrong with the view taken by the Appellate Tribunal that the case filed before the Administrative Tribunal was barred by limitation. 

 12. Mr Sirajul Haque also tried to argue another point that limitation is a mixed question of fact and law. The opposite parties (before the Administrative Tribunal) did not raise any objection before the Administrative Tribunal about the limitation in filing the case before it, therefore, at the appellate stage, they were not entitled to take the said point. It is true that the limitation is a mixed question of fact and law, and that should be taken in the Court of first instance, but there may be cases in which no fact need be gone into and if it is found from the facts stated by the petitioner that a case is filed beyond the period of limitation, particularly in a case under the special statute like the instant one, then we do not find any legal bar to raise the point of limitation even at the appellate stage. When admittedly, the case in hand was filed before the Administrative Tribunal long after the period of six months after the expiry of the period of two months from the date of filing the departmental appeal as provided in the second proviso to sub-section (2) of section 4 of the Act, the opposite parties appellant could very much raise the point of limitation in the appeal and the Appellate Tribunal rightly entertained the same, and decided the point against the petitioner.
